entries.title: Develop before you attack
entries.text: Two of your minor pieces are still at home. An attack launched with half an army is an attack the defender simply outnumbers. Bring the last knight and bishop out first.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Get the king out of the centre
entries.text: You have not castled and the centre can open at any moment. The king in the middle is the reason most short games end early. Castle now, count later.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Punish the uncastled king
entries.text: Their king is still in the centre. Do not drift — open a central file and aim everything at it while it is still standing there.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Do not chase pawns in the opening
entries.text: You are behind in material but the position is still young. Grabbing a second pawn with the queen usually costs three tempi. Finish developing and the pawn comes back.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: A big centre is a target, not a trophy
entries.text: They own two central pawns. That looks impressive and it is also the thing to attack: hit the base with a pawn break rather than admiring it from a distance.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Take the centre while they hesitate
entries.text: You have the central pawns and they do not. Every extra square in the centre is a square their pieces cannot use. Support the centre before you expand on a wing.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Your king cover is gone
entries.text: The pawns in front of your king have left. Before anything else, work out which piece defends the entry squares — and if the answer is none, bring one back.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Their king is the weak point
entries.text: Their pawn shield is broken. Pieces, not pawns, finish this kind of job — count how many attackers you can add against how many defenders they have.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Three attackers means it is real
entries.text: They already have three or more pieces bearing on your king. This is no longer a threat you can answer later. Trade the most dangerous attacker or block the file.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Opposite castling means race
entries.text: Kings on opposite wings: whoever gets there first wins, and defensive moves cost the whole race. Push the pawns in front of their king, not in front of yours.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Do not open lines toward your own king
entries.text: Their king is on the other wing and yours is exposed. Every exchange in front of your king helps them. Keep it closed and attack instead.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Blockade the isolated pawn
entries.text: They have an isolated queen's pawn. Do not try to win it yet — put a knight on the square in front of it. A blockaded isolani defends nothing and attacks nothing.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: The isolani is dynamic, so use it fast
entries.text: You have the isolated queen's pawn. It gives you two open files and active pieces now, and a weakness later. Play for the attack while the pieces are still on.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Trade pieces against the isolani
entries.text: You are playing against the isolated pawn and the endgame is where it actually falls. Every pair of minor pieces you trade makes it weaker.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Do not trade into a lost pawn endgame
entries.text: You have the isolated pawn. Queens and minor pieces are your compensation — trading them leaves you defending a hole in an endgame.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Attack a backward pawn on the file it cannot leave
entries.text: They have a backward pawn that cannot advance. Double rooks on that file. It cannot run and it cannot be defended by a pawn.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Fix the backward pawn before you attack it
entries.text: Your own backward pawn is the target in this structure. Either push it through now while you can, or defend the square in front of it before they occupy it.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Three pawn islands is one too many
entries.text: Your pawns are split into three or more groups. Each island needs its own defender, and in the endgame that is one piece you never get to use. Avoid further trades that fix them.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Doubled pawns are a file, not just a flaw
entries.text: You have doubled pawns. The half-open file they created is the compensation — put a rook on it rather than mourning the structure.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Rooks belong on open files
entries.text: There is an open file and your rook is not on it. That single move is usually worth more than any pawn move available here.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: A rook on the seventh eats pawns
entries.text: Your rook is on the seventh rank. Keep it there. Doubling a second rook behind it is usually stronger than winning a single pawn somewhere else.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Challenge their rook on the seventh
entries.text: Their rook has reached your second rank, where it attacks pawns and the king at once. Offer a trade or block the rank — do not let it sit.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: An outpost is worth a pawn
entries.text: You have a knight sitting where no pawn can ever chase it. Do not trade it off for a passive bishop, and think twice before moving it at all.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Take the outpost square away
entries.text: They have a knight on a square your pawns cannot touch. Trade it, even at the cost of your good bishop — a permanent outpost outlasts any single exchange.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: The bishop pair likes open positions
entries.text: You have both bishops. Open a file or a diagonal rather than closing the position — the pair is worth roughly half a pawn, but only with space to work in.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Close the position against the bishop pair
entries.text: They have both bishops. Fix the pawn chains and keep the knights: a blocked position turns their pair into two large pawns.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: More space means do not trade
entries.text: You control noticeably more of the board. With more space, every exchange helps the cramped side — keep the pieces on and improve your worst one.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Cramped means trade
entries.text: They have more space and your pieces are stepping on each other. Trade a pair of pieces and the position breathes again.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Something of yours is hanging
entries.text: You have a piece that is attacked and undefended. Before any plan, answer this: defend it, move it, or make a bigger threat.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Something of theirs is loose
entries.text: They have a piece hanging. Loose pieces drop off — check every check and capture before you play anything quiet.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: You are in check, so the list is short
entries.text: You are in check. There are only three answers in chess: move the king, block, or take the checker. Look at all three before choosing.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Push the passed pawn
entries.text: You have a passed pawn. In an endgame it is the most valuable thing on the board — every tempo it advances costs them a piece to stop it.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Blockade their passer with the king
entries.text: They have a passed pawn and the pieces are few. The king is the ideal blockader in an endgame: it stops the pawn and keeps working.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Rooks go behind passed pawns
entries.text: Rook endgame with a passed pawn on the board. The rook belongs behind it — yours or theirs. In front of the pawn the rook does nothing.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Activate the king
entries.text: This is an endgame and your king is not doing anything. An active king is worth about a pawn here — walk it toward the action before you start pushing pawns.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Trade pieces, not pawns, when ahead
entries.text: You are ahead in material in an endgame. Trade pieces at every safe opportunity and keep the pawns — a simplified position converts itself.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Keep pieces on when behind
entries.text: You are down material in an endgame. Every trade brings the loss closer. Keep pieces on, create a passed pawn, and make them find moves.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: The isolated pawn finally falls here
entries.text: You are in an endgame against an isolated pawn. This is the phase it was always going to be weak in. Attack it with everything and force them to defend passively.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Ask what they want first
entries.text: Before choosing your move, find the move they would play if it were their turn. Prophylaxis is not passive — it is taking their idea away before it arrives.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Improve the worst piece
entries.text: Nothing is forcing here. When there is no tactic, the strongest move is usually the one that fixes your least useful piece.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Ahead in material means simplify
entries.text: You are up material. Trades favour you now — not pawn trades, piece trades. Head for a position where the extra material is the only thing left on the board.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.

entries.title: Behind in material means complicate
entries.text: You are down material. A quiet position loses slowly and surely. Keep the queens on, aim at the king, and give them chances to go wrong.

source.author: Coach Karlis seed set
source.note: Classical principles, restated for this app and checked against the position before use.
